$comment: §ROW-GATE-REGISTRY — the registration bridge, NOT a second authority.
`bim30-status` decides a row by reading the `check-*` tokens out of the row's
*Deciding instrument* cell in BIM30-MASTER-COMPLETION-TRACKER.md. A row whose cell
names no gate is printed CARRIED: its status is inherited from prose and is not
evidence at HEAD. That is the correct default and it must stay.
This file attaches an EXISTING, RUNNABLE gate to a row whose markdown cell has not
yet been rewritten to name it. It exists because the gate and the prose land through
different review paths here (agents commit scoped code; the tracker prose is edited
centrally), and a gate that is built, registered in run-all.ts, and still invisible to
the status tool is authored-but-unwired in a new costume.
RULES, enforced by the loader in bim30-status.ts and not merely written here:
1. ADD-ONLY. An entry may add gates to a row. It can never remove one the markdown
names, and it can never make a row CARRIED that the markdown would have measured.
2. Every `row` must exist in the tracker. An entry naming a row that does not exist
is a silent no-op, so it is MISCONFIGURED (exit 2) instead.
3. Every gate must resolve to a real file under one of the two gate dirs. Same
reason: a registration pointing at nothing must not read as a registration.
4. Every overlay-registered row is PRINTED as such, with this file named, so no
reader can mistake the markdown for having said it.
`instrumentCellShouldRead` is the exact text the tracker's *Deciding instrument* cell
should adopt, so reconciling the prose is mechanical rather than a re-derivation. Each
string is fed through the tool's OWN `extractGates` on every run and must yield exactly
the `gates` array beside it — otherwise pasting it into the doc would silently change
which gate decides the row, which is precisely the failure this file must not cause.
This registry does NOT carry statuses, readings, counts or baselines. It carries the
name of the instrument and nothing else. It is not a debt ledger.

entries.why: The cell read 'source re-measure of the four families' and the reading cell read NOT DETERMINED. CV1 counts the three C73 §0.2 families on the axis each was actually duplicated along — FILE for WallIntersectionResolver and FloorPlanDiagnostics (neither declares a class, so a class census reads 0 and passes over live copies), CLASS for RoomStore (fixed by renaming the class and KEEPING the filename, so a filename census reads 2 forever).
entries.instrumentCellShouldRead: `check-census-verified-invariants` CV1 — the three C73 §0.2 duplicate families each resolve to ONE production authority, counted on the axis each was duplicated along

entries.why: The cell read '`polygonBoolean.ts` + its oracle suite' — two artefacts and no way to run them. The gate asserts a UNION ENTRY POINT is exported (an intersection-only kernel still cannot merge two footprints), that the oracle is claimed by an include glob, and it SPAWNS the oracle, flooring on tests EXECUTED.
entries.instrumentCellShouldRead: `check-polygon-boolean-canonical` — the union entry point is EXPORTED (not merely mentioned), the oracle suite is claimed by an include glob, and it executes green with a floor on tests executed

entries.why: The cell read '`SplitWall.ts` + the verb register'. CV2 asserts three facts, because any one alone is satisfiable by a stub: a handler declares `type = 'wall.split'`, the plugin's type list contains the id, and the handler is CONSTRUCTED. An id listed with no handler is GE-06's defect, one row up the same table.
entries.instrumentCellShouldRead: `check-census-verified-invariants` CV2 — `wall.split` is declared by a handler, listed by the wall type register, AND constructed into the handler set

entries.why: The cell read 'source re-measure' and the reading cell read NOT DETERMINED. CV3 is a hard 0 on `createWorkerHandler` in production source — the row's terminal state was DELETE, and the arm keeps it deleted.
entries.instrumentCellShouldRead: `check-census-verified-invariants` CV3 — `createWorkerHandler` stays at its DELETE terminal state: zero production occurrences

entries.why: The cell read 'source census', reading not itemised. CV4 asserts ONE production declaration of `StairValidationAuthority` AND at least one production importer that is not a barrel — the row's own complaint is about a copy with zero importers, so counting authorities alone would miss half of it.
entries.instrumentCellShouldRead: `check-census-verified-invariants` CV4 — exactly one `StairValidationAuthority` authority, with a production importer that is not a re-export barrel

entries.why: The cell read 'source census of `provideLiveGraphSources` callers'. CV5 counts production call sites and files test-only callers separately — a dev-only caller is the defect this row names, not its refutation. The call is not dot-prefixed, so `check-source-verified-invariants`' SV5 detector is structurally blind to it.
entries.instrumentCellShouldRead: `check-census-verified-invariants` CV5 — `provideLiveGraphSources` has a PRODUCTION call site outside its defining file; test-only callers are counted separately and never credited

entries.why: The cell read 'the serializer's `provenance` slice + suite'. There are TWO serialiser/loader pairs and the cited suite pins only the persistence-client one: breaking the APP copy's hydrate leaves that suite green at 11/11 (measured). S1/S2 read BOTH pairs and require the write to be CONDITIONAL, because an unwired bootstrap writing an empty slice over a real audit log is I-INV-3.
entries.instrumentCellShouldRead: `check-provenance-slice-persisted` — BOTH ProjectSerializer copies write the slice conditionally and BOTH ProjectLoader copies hydrate it, plus the cited suite executes; the cited suite alone pins only the L3 copy

entries.why: The cell read 'schema census'. E1 re-derives the census independently from `SCHEMA_REGISTRY`; E2 is the arm that matters — the cited suite derives IN_SCOPE from its own OUT_OF_SCOPE list, so moving a kind into that list with a plausible sentence keeps every assertion green over a smaller subject. E2 pins the exemption list to the five kinds on the record: growth is a finding, shrinkage is not.
entries.instrumentCellShouldRead: `check-element-confidence-declared` — every registered element kind outside the five recorded exemptions declares `confidence`, the exemption list has not grown, and the cited suite executes

deliberatelyUnregisteredComment: Rows examined and left CARRIED ON PURPOSE. This section attaches no gate and never
will; it exists so the next lane does not 'helpfully' gate one of them and mint a
breach the register can never absorb.
The shape is the same in all three cases. These rows are LEGITIMATELY OPEN — the
capability they name is absent, and absent CORRECTLY. Both gate shapes available are
• hard-0 (`declared: 0`) — the defect stands, so findings >= 1, so the gate exits 3.
Exit 3 is RATCHET EXCEEDED and is NEVER absorbable (C70 §5.1). That mints a
permanent breach for a row that is behaving as designed.
• a declared level > 0 — that is a tolerated-failure baseline, i.e. minting debt for
A third shape was considered and rejected for each: asserting something adjacent that
IS currently true (e.g. 'the unimplemented verbs refuse BY NAME') would exit 0 and make
the register print the row CLOSED. The row would then read as resolved while the
capability it names is still missing — which is the exact defect this whole register
exists to remove, committed by the instrument meant to remove it.
Leaving them carried, with the reason, is the correct answer.

deliberatelyUnregistered.why: `planegcs` is a dependency of no workspace, and C74 §4.5 FORBIDS solver work until a constraint family proves it needs solving. The cheapest next action is correctly none. The row's instrument (`grep '"planegcs"' --include=package.json`) is mechanically runnable and would read 0 hits — but a gate over it exits 0, which prints the row CLOSED, asserting a solver capability that does not exist and is not authorised to exist.

Blocked on CO-08 reaching §4.2(c) with evidence: one family has evidence, the rest do not. The instrument names 'one executable test naming `StairValidationAuthority` at its declared VALIDATION strength' — a test that is deliberately not written yet. Gating hard-0 mints an exit-3 breach for a deferral that is correct.

Eleven of the twelve declared clash verbs still have no detector, so the row is correctly OPEN and a hard-0 gate would mint an exit-3 breach. ⚠ Its printed READING is nonetheless stale and should be corrected centrally: the cell says '0 clash-engine implementations; `clash-run` remains a registered id with no handler', but at HEAD §GE-06-ROOF-WALL-WIRE gives `clash-run` a real roof x wall detector, `IMPLEMENTED_CLASH_COMMAND_IDS` in packages/command-bus/src/clashCapability.ts reads ['clash-run'], and apps/editor/__tests__/RoofWallClashVerbReach.test.ts drives it through a real bus. The honest reading is 1 of 12, not 0 of 12. A grow-only ratchet on that count is the natural instrument once someone is authorised to declare a floor.
